text: Read carefully the poem on page 3. It is written by a young poet who became a soldier in the
Second World War.
How does the poet portray himself in this poem?
To help you answer this question, you might consider:
• how he portrays the ways in which war has changed him
• how he conveys his fears
• the ways in which he creates a powerful impression on the reader.
War Poet
I am the man who looked for peace and found
My own eyes barbed .
I am the man who groped for words and found
An arrow in my hand.
I am the builder whose firm walls surround
A slipping land.
When I grow sick or mad
Mock me not nor chain me;
When I reach for the wind
Cast me not down
Though my face is a burnt book
And a wasted town.
barbed: sharply spiked

Read carefully the following extract from a novel set in an imaginary future. Most of the USA
has become a religious dictatorship called Gilead. There are very limited rights for women. The
narrator, Lydia, is explaining how she was forced to surrender to male domination.
How does the writer make this such a disturbing moment in her novel?
To help you answer this question, you might consider:
• the women’s shocked responses at the start of the extract
• the arrival and attitudes of the armed men
• the reactions of Lydia and the other women to the developing situation.
‘We need to get out of the country.
